summary: Control-plane timeouts after TGW route update due to stale VPC DNS cache on customer's resolver
description:
Issue summary:
BrightBank's private deployment started seeing control-plane timeouts and model pull failures after a Transit Gateway (TGW) route table change at ~2026-03-10 02:10 UTC. Symptoms included 504/524 style timeouts from Redwood control-plane calls (model pull, config fetch) and client streaming sessions entering 'Connecting' state for ~30–90s before failing. Impact: production traffic affected for multiple teams; some streaming sessions dropped mid-response.

Impact:
- Intermittent model pull failures causing cold-starts to fail for ~15% of requests for 2 hours.
- Increased tail latency on streaming APIs (median unaffected, 99th percentile increased).
- Customer reported degraded user experience and opened support SLA escalation.

Environment:
- Private deployment in BrightBank VPCs (acct: 123456789012).
- TGW attachments include spoke VPCs and a corporate on-prem VPN.
- Customer uses an EC2-based DNS forwarder (BIND) for VPC resolver caching and has an internal firewall/NACL configuration.

Initial customer-provided details:
- Timing: problem started immediately after a TGW route rewrite to redirect a CIDR to a new spoke.
- Observed behavior: control-plane endpoints intermittently timed out; TLS handshakes occasionally reset.
- No recent changes on Redwood side per console.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Apply TGW route change that moves 10.0.64.0/18 from spoke-A to spoke-B (customer step).
2) Wait ~30–120s for route propagation.
3) Attempt to start a model pull / API request to hosted control-plane endpoints.
4) Observe intermittent timeouts and TCP resets from the control plane IPs.
steps_to_reproduce: Apply TGW route update that rewrites target attachment for a CIDR
Attempt model pull or control-plane request immediately after update
logs: 2026-03-10T02:12:05Z ERR control-plane: dial tcp 10.12.45.9:443: i/o timeout
2026-03-10T02:12:07Z WARN serving-runtime: model pull retry limit reached for model redwood-base-7b
Customer BIND logs: query for control-plane.redwood.example A -> NXDOMAIN cached at 02:11:10
investigation_notes: Checked Redwood control-plane: healthy; no deploys at the incident time
Observed customer reported BIND resolver returning cached NXDOMAIN or old A records for control-plane endpoints after TGW rewrite
Packet captures from customer show SYN->SYN/ACK sometimes, but TLS handshake aborted when routed through old spoke path which blackholed return packets
Customer NACL had ephemeral port range restricted on the spoke that previously hosted the CIDR; when traffic briefly routed to that spoke return traffic failed

Hypothesis: customer resolver cached negative or stale DNS pointing to control-plane IPs reachable via old spoke; ephemeral port block caused TLS resets; combination produced intermittent timeouts until cache TTL expired
comments: Asha Patel (Support): Customer reports timeouts started after TGW route change; requested immediate triage and workaround guidance.
Evelyn Chang (SRE): Requested packet captures and BIND query logs; asked customer to flush resolver cache and check NACL ephemeral port rules.
BrightBank NetOps (customer): Confirmed they had a short TTL but BIND had negative-caching set to 300s; flushed cache at 02:25 UTC and reported immediate reduction in failures.
Evelyn Chang (SRE): Verified control-plane metrics returned to baseline after cache flush; recommended permanent fix and follow-ups.
root_cause_summary: Customer's EC2-based DNS forwarder (BIND) cached stale negative/old A records for Redwood control-plane hostnames after a TGW route rewrite. Some requests were routed to the old spoke where NACLs blocked ephemeral return ports, causing TLS handshake failures and timeouts. The combination of stale DNS entries and network ACL restrictions produced intermittent control-plane timeouts until cache was flushed and NACLs corrected.
resolution: Worked with customer to flush the resolver cache and temporarily increase negative-caching TTL tolerance. Customer adjusted NACL ephemeral port rules on the old spoke to allow return traffic. After cache flush at 2026-03-10T02:25 UTC and NACL relaxation, control-plane failures subsided and metrics normalized by 2026-03-10T02:40 UTC.
postmortem_actions: Customer to set negative-caching (NXDOMAIN) to <=60s for internal forwarder or enable short positive TTLs for control-plane hostnames
Add a guidance note in Private Deploy runbook about TGW route changes and DNS caching implications
Support to create a check-list for customers doing TGW route rewrites recommending resolver cache flush and ephemeral port verification
Engineering follow-up: consider adding a detector in Console/Optimize that warns when private deployments report resolver NXDOMAINs during topology changes
resolution_notes: Temporary: cache flush and NACL relaxation performed by customer.
Permanent: customer adjusted TTLs and updated runbooks; file closed after verification period.
No code changes required on Redwood side; recommend doc update and monitoring enhancement.
